hints: Focus on what each reagent actually reacts with, sodium reacts with both alcohols and carboxylic acids, but carbonate only reacts with acids.
Remember the mole ratios, one mole of -OH or -COOH gives 0.5 mol of H2 with Na, while one mole of -COOH gives 0.5 mol of CO2 with carbonate.
Count the alcohol and acid groups in each structure and check where total H2 moles equals total CO2 moles.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two gas-forming reactions**

Sodium gives hydrogen with any acidic proton from an alcohol or a carboxylic acid. Carbonate gives carbon dioxide only with the stronger carboxylic acid.

$$2\text{ROH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{RONa} + \text{H}_2$$
$$2\text{RCOOH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{RCOONa} + \text{H}_2$$
$$2\text{RCOOH} + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow 2\text{RCOONa} + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Turn groups into moles of gas**

For 1 mole of compound, each -OH or -COOH makes 0.5 mol $\text{H}_2$ with excess Na. Each -COOH makes 0.5 mol $\text{CO}_2$ with excess carbonate.

$$\text{mol H}_2 = 0.5 \times (\text{number of alcohol OH} + \text{number of COOH})$$
$$\text{mol CO}_2 = 0.5 \times (\text{number of COOH})$$

**Count groups and compare**

A is $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ with 2 alcohols, so 1.0 mol $\text{H}_2$ but 0 mol $\text{CO}_2$. B has 1 alcohol plus 1 acid, so 1.0 mol $\text{H}_2$ but 0.5 mol $\text{CO}_2$. C has 1 alcohol plus 1 aldehyde, so 0.5 mol $\text{H}_2$ but 0 mol $\text{CO}_2$.

Only the dicarboxylic acid $\text{HOOC-COOH}$ has 2 acids and no alcohols, so $\text{H}_2 = 0.5 \times 2 = 1.0$ mol and $\text{CO}_2 = 0.5 \times 2 = 1.0$ mol. Equal volumes, so that is the answer.

options.A: This is ethane-1,2-diol with two alcohol groups. With Na it gives 1 mol H2, but alcohols do not react with Na2CO3 so it gives 0 mol CO2. Volumes are different.
options.B: This is 2-hydroxypropanoic acid with one alcohol and one carboxylic acid. With Na it gives 0.5 + 0.5 = 1 mol H2, but with carbonate only the one acid counts, giving 0.5 mol CO2. Volumes are different.
options.C: This is HOCH2CHO with one alcohol and one aldehyde. With Na it gives 0.5 mol H2, but neither group reacts with carbonate to give gas, so 0 mol CO2. Volumes are different.
options.D: This is ethanedioic acid, HOOC-COOH, with two carboxylic acid groups. With Na, 1 mol gives 1 mol H2. With Na2CO3, 1 mol gives 1 mol CO2. The gas volumes are the same.
